subject: Audit warroom kickoff — log access playbook & JIT procedures
messages:
From: markus.klein@redwood.ai
To: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai, olga.petrov@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: carla.mendoza@independent-audit.com
Date: Wed, 7 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Audit warroom kickoff — log access playbook & JIT procedures

Team —

Per our timeline with Acme (SIG + FedRAMP readiness scope), auditor intake is next week and they asked for a concrete runbook for how we will provide log samples and short-lived access during interviews. I put a first-draft runbook in the Drive folder (link below) and attached a printable summary. Key asks we need to align on: 

- Owner for auditor-facing JIT accounts (name + pager)
- Exact log types and retention windows we will hand over (SIEM/ELB/db/worker)
- Method for redaction of PII before handover and the review gate (security + legal)
- Network/console access method: SAML-brokered temporary role vs. bastion jumpbox
- Evidence artifacts to attach to the runbook (screenshots, session recordings, signed access consent)

Please review the runbook PDF and the log-sample-manifest.csv I added. Kimberly: can you confirm the retention windows and the export process for CloudWatch/ELB/OS logs? Jonas: propose a JIT role name and TTL policy we can present to auditors. Olga: advise on the redaction checklist and whether the SIEM export needs offline hash-redaction steps. Marcus — copying Marissa for audit coordination and escalation path.

Goal: have a polished runbook and assigned owners by EOD tomorrow so I can send to Carla before the pre-intake call.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AuditWarroomRunbook

Thanks,
Markus Klein
VP, Infrastructure & Security
Redwood Inference

Attachment: audit-warroom-runbook-v1.pdf (summary runbook, 6 pages)
Attachment: log-sample-manifest.csv (10 lines)
From: kimberly.park@redwood.ai
To: markus.klein@redwood.ai
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, olga.petrov@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, carla.mendoza@independent-audit.com
Date: Wed, 7 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Audit warroom kickoff — log access playbook & JIT procedures

Thanks, Mark. Quick answers inline: 

- Retention windows: ELB access logs (90 days), CloudWatch consolidated logs (365 days for security-relevant streams, 30 days for app debug). Database slow query logs retained 180 days. I updated the manifest with exact S3 prefixes.
- Export process: We will use a Lambda batch exporter that writes manifests to a secure S3 bucket with access-scoped prefixes. For bulk sampling we produce gz archives and a manifest CSV (see attached sample).
- Format: CSV manifest has object key, start/end timestamps, SHA256 hash, and minimal PII flag.

Action items for me: confirm S3 lifecycle rule won't delete required sample during the audit window (will set a hold for 14 days past the auditor sign-off).

Questions: Do auditors require live console sessions for SIEM triage or are static samples acceptable? If live sessions are needed, we should use a time-bound SAML role + session recording.

-Kimberly
Director, Cloud Ops

Attachment: log-sample-manifest.csv (updated)

Subject: Re: Audit warroom kickoff — log access playbook & JIT procedures

Markus/Kimberly —

Thanks for the draft. A few clarifying points from the audit team: 

1) Static samples are preferred initially (manifests + gz archives). We'll request live console access only for sessions where we need to validate triage behavior or reproduce an incident timeline.

2) For live access, we require: a unique temporary identity per auditor (no shared accounts), MFA enforced, session recording stored to a write-once bucket, and an access consent document signed by Acme's security officer. DocuSign is fine.

3) Redaction: we can accept hashed PII in the manifest, but the auditors will need the original identifiers for a small sample (up to 10 items) under an NDA. Provide a process to request those with a documented approval trail.

4) Timing: we will need the first static samples 48 hours before the intake call. Please ensure the S3 manifests and credentials are ready by Monday 10/12 09:00 PT.

I'll join the pre-intake call; please include a brief 10-min run-through of the runbook.

Regards,
Carla Mendoza
Lead Auditor
Independent Audit LLP

Folks —

Nice alignment. Quick status and owners: 

- Kimberley: you own static sample exports and manifest delivery (deliver by 2026-10-12T09:00-07:00).
- Jonas Weber: owner for JIT role and session policy. Proposed role: "auditor_jit_readonly" TTL 4 hours, MFA required, session recording to s3://redwood-audit-recordings/ (retained 90 days). Please create the role and a runbook snippet for the pre-intake demo.
- Olga Petrov: redaction gate owner. Please publish a one-page checklist for the legal/security approval flow; include who can unmask for the small-sample exceptions.
- Marissa Cole: point-of-contact for escalation during auditor sessions; you will hold the pager for the intake window 10/12-10/16.

Carla: we will have the sample manifest and two archive bundles uploaded by the deadline. I'll send the DocuSign access-consent to Acme's SecOps and to your team this afternoon.

Next steps: Jonas, Kimberly, Olga — please drop the runbook snippets into the Drive under the 'runbook/live-snippets' folder and ping me when done. Once I have owners confirmed I'll send a single-runbook PDF to Carla.

Thanks everyone — feeling good about the plan.

Best,
Markus
VP, Infrastructure & Security

Attachment: audit-warroom-runbook-v1.pdf (updated with owners)
